question.text: The operations head of Nalanda Venture Fund is mapping service-provider responsibilities. Which function is MOST directly the responsibility of the Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) of an AIF?

answer.text: Conducting valuation of unlisted securities in the scheme's portfolio.
Maintaining the unit-holder register, processing subscriptions/redemptions, unit transfers, and acting as collecting agent for stamp duty on issuance/transfer of AIF units.
Signing the PPM due diligence certificate submitted to SEBI.
Appointing the statutory auditor at the AGM.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7, RTAs oversee 'issue of new class of units, partly-paid units, transfer of units, full and partial redemption calls, payment of exit load, expenses and fees by the selling unit holder'. They were also notified as 'collecting agents' for stamp duty on AIF units (SEBI circular dated 30-Jun-2020) — making RTA appointment compulsory. The Trap: Option A is the valuer's job. Option C is the merchant banker's function. Option D is a Board/trustee governance decision. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests RTA from a distributor-onboarding view. Mutual-fund-side exams (V-A) cover RTAs similarly — but AIF RTA additionally handles stamp-duty collection, which MF RTAs also do but under a separate circular stream. Manager's Pro-Tip: Reconcile the RTA register against the custodian holdings and the fund administrator's NAV every month — any break between these three is your first signal of an operational error or fraud.
